title: A Gate That Cannot Fail Is Not a Gate

intelligence.essence: Every gate in this block earns its authority the same way: by being able to fail, on the exact thing it guards, proven before it is trusted. A promotion gate admitted tampered lessons until its proof was bound to the capture's canonical bytes (SN-837); a governance check written in grep fired on the clean tree itself because text cannot tell a definition from an import (SN-888); a credential check passed *absence* because a truthy guard short-circuited it (SN-859); eight directives were reported "built" with zero enforced, because code existence is not enforcement existence (SN-940). The craft rules that follow — survey the data before encoding the gate (SN-846), straddle every threshold in time (SN-820), probe adversarial phrasings (SN-845), fix at the canonical seam (SN-818), never bind authority to a recyclable `id()` (SN-935), write the expected-FAIL fixture first (SN-1167) — are one law in fourteen work clothes: **an instrument that cannot say no has said nothing.**
intelligence.human_view: This is the block's workshop manual for locks. A lock is only a lock if it can refuse to open. Again and again the team found "protections" that could not refuse: a stamp that approved tampered goods, a guard that shouted at the wrong people and would have let the right ones through, a checklist that waved empty hands through, code that existed but was never switched on. Each time, the fix was the same shape — make the thing prove it can say no, on the real goods, before anyone trusts its yes.
intelligence.child_view: A gate is like a teacher checking your homework. If the teacher says "good job!" no matter what you hand in — even if you hand in your friend's homework, or no homework at all — the "good job" means nothing. A real check has to be able to say "no, that's wrong." So before we trust any checker, we test it: we hand it something wrong on purpose, and it has to catch it.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's the difference between a lock and a picture of a lock, dear. These notes are full of pictures that hung on doors for weeks — checks that approved everything, alarms that cried at the wrong house. The craft here is plain: try the lock with the wrong key before you trust it with the right one, write down that you tried, and never let a label do a lock's job.
intelligence.ai_view: Bind every proof to canonical bytes + digest and re-derive expected values from the artifact itself (SN-837). Grep your own gates for the `if x and x != EXPECTED` signature and for comments claiming enforcement the code path doesn't perform (SN-859, SN-860). Implement construct-detection with AST and ship both controls with the guard (SN-888). Straddle thresholds — time, phrasing, offsets — in every falsifier suite (SN-820, SN-845); survey the corpus before encoding corpus gates (SN-846). Patch the shared seam, verify the caller actually invokes the checker (SN-818), and keep execution under the plan's own rulebook (SN-828). Receipt hook failures without flipping outcomes (SN-877); model pending as its own state (SN-857); audit any `id()` in authority logic on sight (SN-935). Report SPEC-ONLY until violation + path + observed FAIL are all named (SN-940), and write the FAIL fixture before the PASS fixtures (SN-1167).
intelligence.what_it_means: Fourteen notes, one epistemology of machinery: the value of a gate is exactly its demonstrated ability to refuse. Every defect class here — vacuous success, short-circuited absence, text-matched structure, uninvoked checker, recycled identity, unenforced "built" code — is a different way for a yes to be worthless. A cold reader holding only this essence can audit any gate in the system with five questions: what does it bind to, can absence pass it, does it parse or pattern-match, who invokes it, and where is its observed failure?
whats_inside: Proof binds to canonical bytes and claimed digests, not to labels; skipped decisive jobs make a SUCCESS vacuous (SN-837).
Absence must fail checks, not skip them: the `if x and x != EXPECTED` signature is a defect class, closed before wiring lands (SN-859); comments claiming unperformed enforcement are defects (SN-860).

Code-construct guards parse structure (AST), never grep text, and pass a positive *and* a negative control before wiring (SN-888); falsifiers straddle thresholds in time and phrasing (SN-820, SN-845).
Gates are designed to surveyed reality (598/606), documented so they are not "fixed" back to the ideal (SN-846).
Repairs land at the canonical seam; an uninvoked checker enforces nothing (SN-818); execution re-checks under the plan's own rulebook (SN-828).
Hooks observe and receipt, never decide (SN-877); instruments model pending as a third state (SN-857).
Authority identity is a monotonic UUID, never `id()` (SN-935).
"Built" without an observed FAIL on violation is SPEC-ONLY (SN-940); the expected-FAIL fixture is written and run first (SN-1167).
